title: Fine-Tuning LLMs Without Breaking Your Laptop
subtitle: How quantization and tiny adapters make big models personal
intro: A giant language model knows everything, but not your job. What if you could teach it your style on one GPU?
takeaway: Fine-tuning adds a tiny, trainable adapter to a shrunken model so it learns your task cheaply.

sections.heading: Analogy: the frozen chef and the sticky note
sections.body:
Think of a pre-trained LLM as a master chef who already knows every recipe. You don't retrain the chef from scratch.

You freeze the chef and just add a sticky note with your tweaks. That sticky note is LoRA, a Low-Rank Adaptation. It is a small add-on you train instead of the whole model.

This idea is called PEFT, Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning, and it leads to why we do it this way.

sections.heading: Why it exists: make it small enough to teach
sections.body:
A full model is too big for most computers. Quantization with bitsandbytes shrinks it from 16-bit to 4-bit so it fits in memory.

Then you format your data into prompt templates and train only the LoRA adapter with SFTTrainer from Hugging Face. You get a custom assistant you can run locally with Ollama.

Cheap and local sounds perfect, but shrinking and shortcuts have costs.

sections.heading: What can go wrong: when the shortcut fails
sections.body:
If your dataset formatting is messy, the adapter learns the wrong pattern and repeats it.

If you quantize too aggressively, the model loses accuracy and gives fuzzy answers. And a tiny LoRA cannot fix a base model that never knew your domain.

So check your data and test the shrunken model before you trust it.

steps.narration: Start with a frozen pre-trained LLM.
Shrink it with bitsandbytes quantization to fit your GPU.
Attach a small trainable LoRA adapter.
Train just the adapter on your formatted dataset with SFTTrainer.
Deploy the combined model locally with Ollama.

quiz.q: What does LoRA do in PEFT?
options: Retrains every parameter of the base model
Adds a small trainable adapter while freezing the base model
Deletes the base model to save space
quiz.why: LoRA freezes the big model and trains only a tiny low-rank adapter, which is the core of PEFT.

quiz.q: Why use quantization with bitsandbytes before fine-tuning?
options: To make the model larger and slower
To shrink the model to 4-bit so it fits on limited GPU memory
To deploy to Ollama without training
quiz.why: Quantization reduces memory use so you can load and fine-tune a large model on a single consumer GPU.

quiz.q: What breaks first if you fine-tune on a messy, poorly formatted dataset?
options: The LoRA adapter learns and repeats the wrong patterns
quiz.why: The adapter only learns what you show it; bad formatting teaches bad behavior that persists after deployment.

extra: QLoRA combines 4-bit quantization with LoRA to fine-tune 65B models on a single 48GB GPU.
